grade.reason: brief instruction: match starter's darkness (graded floor L ~21.7) while keeping bone's own hue/chroma readable (not flattened toward starter's umber)
grade.tool: postprocess.py grade -- ONE (l_offset, chroma_scale) transform in CIE Lab derived from ONE sample-vs-reference comparison, applied identically to every tile in the family
grade.referenceConstruction: no bone-specific approved spike existed to sample a reference crop from (unlike starter, which had mock-A2.png), so the reference was constructed synthetically: measured the sample's own mean Lab (L=47.75, mean a=1.23, mean b=7.26, hue ~80.4deg, chroma magnitude 7.365 -- the floor's hue is very consistent pixel-to-pixel, so the vector-mean hue ~= the scalar-mean chroma direction), then built an 8x8 solid-colour swatch at Lab(L=21.7, same chroma magnitude 7.365, same hue angle) and used that as --ref. Because apply_grade scales each pixel's own (a,b) by a uniform chroma_scale (hue-preserving per pixel, not remapped to the reference's hue), this reference choice makes the transform match starter's TARGET DARKNESS while leaving the transform's own resulting chroma_scale close to 1.0 (own saturation preserved, not flattened) -- directly matching the brief's instruction to keep the biome's own hue/chroma read able.
grade.appliedTo: all 16 rock tiles and all 5 floor variants (21 tiles) -- not applied to stamps (they keep their own accent colours, per controller ruling R3 in starter's chosen.json)

highlightCompress.reason: the raw rock corner-set tiles baked in an uneven, fairly bright dust-cloud/highlight artifact on several (not all) of the 16 masks' floor portions -- literal fallout of the floor prompt ('dusted with pale bone dust') but distributed inconsistently across masks (raw p95 luma as high as L=90 on some tiles, as low as L=55 on others), so tiling several different masks next to each other in a room made the highlight read as a patchy, semi-random glowing-cloud artifact rather than a deliberate accent. A full reroll was considered but rejected (stochastic, not guaranteed to fix, and the underlying 'dusted floor' concept is correct per the recipe) in favour of a zero-spend, pipeline-only fix, the same category as starter's 'fill' step.
highlightCompress.tool: ad hoc script (not a postprocess.py subcommand) using postprocess.py's own _rgb_to_lab_one/_lab_to_rgb_one: for every pixel with Lab L above a knee, compress the excess above the knee by a fixed ratio, alpha and a/b untouched (hue-preserving, only tames how bright the brightest highlights get)
highlightCompress.appliedTo: all 16 graded rock tiles only (not floor variants or stamps) -- e.g. a raw graded pixel that would have landed at L=64 lands at L=25+(64-25)*0.4=40.6; pixels at or below the base floor's own L (~21.7) are untouched
highlightCompress.verification: room mockup before/after: before, pale near-white cloud shapes appeared repeatedly around every straight wall edge and around both pillars, reading as a lighting/glow artifact; after, the same areas read as a subtle rubble/dust scatter at the wall base, consistent with the recipe's 'dusted with pale bone dust' floor description -- no longer looks like a defect

floorHaloFix.reason: user review: 'Pale bone-dust blotches ring every wall and pillar edge because the floor half of the rock corner tiles doesn't match the plain floor tile.' Requested waiting for the crystal agent's new `postprocess.py unifyfloor` subcommand rather than writing a competing fix.
floorHaloFix.waitedFor: python3 scripts/tiles/postprocess.py unifyfloor --help -- already existed on first check (no polling wait needed).
floorHaloFix.tool: postprocess.py unifyfloor -- classifies each rock-corner-tile pixel by Lab colour distance to a small palette built from the floor-ref tile; pixels within tolerance get replaced pixel-for-pixel with the SAME-POSITION floor-ref pixel (not palette_match/recolour), pixels outside tolerance (presumed rock/edge) are left untouched; a morphology pass protects small isolated same-colour flecks (e.g. bone-yellow skull highlights that happen to be Lab-close to the floor palette) from being swept even though their raw distance passes
floorHaloFix.pipelineOrder: re-derived the pre-highlight-compress graded rock tiles from raw (deterministic, same grade transform, zero spend), re-applied the SAME highlight-compress pass documented above (so the approved look is the starting point, not a fresh generation), re-repaired the seam on the compressed pure-floor tile, THEN ran unifyfloor on all 16 compressed tiles using that same compressed+repaired tile_15 as --floor-ref, THEN re-checked the seam on the unifyfloor'd tile_15 (a no-op there: unifyfloor replaced 0/576 of tile_15's own pixels since it IS the floor-ref, so no discontinuity was introduced and no further repair was needed).
floorHaloFix.toleranceChoice: the tool's default --tolerance 9 barely changed the visible halo (e.g. mask 3/raw tile_3: 66.8% of floor-region pixels replaced by count, but the specific pale outlier pixels causing the visible blotch were UNTOUCHED -- their Lab distance from the floor palette, ~10-14 at the brightest sampled points, was close to but under the classification boundary only for the least-bright halo pixels). Diagnosed the actual Lab-distance-to-floor-palette gap directly: the rock's own darkest mortar pixels sit at distance ~16.4-16.8 from the floor palette, while the brightest halo pixels sampled were at ~14.4 -- i.e. the halo is CLOSER to the floor palette than genuine rock mortar is, but both are close enough together that there's a narrow safe window. Binary-searched it: tolerance 16 removes nearly all of the visible halo (checked per-tile replaced-pixel counts, all comfortably under the danger zone) while tolerance 18 crosses the cliff and starts replacing genuine dark rock/mortar pixels too (one test tile jumped from 66% to 98.8% replaced and visually lost all its skull/mortar texture, becoming indistinguishable from floor). Shipped with --tolerance 16 (all other params left at default: --palette-colors 12, --min-speck 3, --min-hole 3).
floorHaloFix.verification: room mockup before/after, by eye: before, pale cloud shapes rang every straight wall edge and both pillars; after, floor reads uniformly right up to the rock edge everywhere in the mockup room, no visible halo. Re-ran postprocess.py seam on the final tile_15 (unchanged from the pre-unifyfloor check, since unifyfloor made no change to that specific tile): band_score col=0.215 row=0.200, both under the 1.0 threshold.
